title: Pharmacy relations: transfer, mail-order and specialty dispensing by prescription class
content:
**To retail, mail-order and specialty pharmacies filling Prescriptions & Renewals prescriptions.** For each class, Linden Ridge sets whether the remaining fills may be moved to another pharmacy, whether only one such move is permitted over the prescription's life, whether a designated specialty pharmacy must fill it, whether it may be filled by mail order and the days' supply of a mail-order fill.

| Class | Remaining fills may move to another pharmacy | Only one move over the prescription's life | Designated specialty pharmacy required | Mail order allowed | Mail-order fill (days' supply) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acute Short-Course Prescription | yes | no | no | no | 0 |
| Standard Maintenance Prescription | yes | no | no | yes | 90 |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription | yes | no | no | yes | 90 |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | yes | yes | no | yes | 30 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | no | no | no | no | 0 |
| Specialty Medication Prescription | no | no | yes | yes | 30 |

**Notes.**

- A mail-order fill of 0 days means mail order is not available for the class.
- The Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription is the only class limited to one pharmacy move over its life.
- The Schedule II Controlled Prescription and the Specialty Medication Prescription are marked "no" for moving remaining fills; the Specialty Medication Prescription must be filled by a designated specialty pharmacy.
- Mail-order fills dispense 90 days for both maintenance classes and 30 days for the Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription and the Specialty Medication Prescription.
